text:
maria: heads-up, ACME Prod (dedicated pool x-prod-1) reported a sudden throughput drop ~14:03 UTC. Calls started getting 429s and p95 shot up from 180ms to ~1.2s. customer says this started after we rolled the scheduler tweak yesterday.

sam: any error traces or sample req ids? 429 usually indicates throttling but could be small micro-batches.

maria: copied a few request ids from the support logs: req=01f3a2, 01f3a8, 01f3b0. support-bot shows burst of short requests from their tenant around the same time.

lee: can you run the diagnostics script on the node? quick check: `curl -s http://metrics.internal/pools/x-prod-1/summary | jq .`

maria: ran that, here's the relevant bits (trimmed):
```
{"pool":"x-prod-1","active_workers":8,"avg_batch_size":1.9,"max_batch_tokens":32,"continuous_batcher_queue_depth":240,"scheduler_swaps":78}
```

jess: avg_batch_size 1.9 is suspicious for our workloads — sounds like token-sorting or a prefill check is forcing many tiny batches. Did the new scheduler change token-sorting order?

maria: config diff from yesterday has `scheduler.preemptive_swap=true` and a tweak to `token_sort: adaptive`. I think adaptive started re-ordering by token_count, but for ACME their traffic is many short prompts and a bunch of medium responses so it fragments.

dinesh: I saw a similar oscillation in canary — scheduler kept swapping in/out micro-batchers to try to improve latency, but it caused starvation for continuous-batcher and prevented prefix caching from being effective. That reduces throughput even though workers are 'busy'.

sam: can you repro locally with the same traffic mix? quick repro steps: 1) run `tools/loadgen --tenant acme --rps 120 --mix short:0.8,medium:0.2` 2) set `scheduler.preemptive_swap=true` 3) observe `avg_batch_size` and `p95`

maria: starting loadgen now. attaching a short snippet of the scheduler log around the time it degrades: 
```
[14:03:12] scheduler: allocate group=continuous-batcher worker=3 tokens=16
[14:03:12] scheduler: preempt swap -> micro-batcher-5 (expected_batch=4)
[14:03:13] worker[3]: process start req=01f3a2 tokens=8
[14:03:13] kvcache: miss prefix=abcd
[14:03:14] scheduler: evict group=continuous-batcher -> avg_batch_size now 1.1
[14:03:15] throttle: 429 tenant=acme reason=queue_quota
```

jess: looks like preemptive swapping is fragmenting the queue and preventing effective batching and cache reuse. Also note `queue_quota` throttle — the token accounting code might be charging per-request too aggressively when batch sizes drop.

lee: immediate mitigations: 1) roll back `scheduler.preemptive_swap` on x-prod-1 2) bump `min_batch_size=4` for continuous-batcher policy 3) temporarily increase tenant queue quota for ACME to clear the backlog.

sam: agree. Also add a metric alert for `avg_batch_size < 2` to detect early.

maria: rollback started on pool x-prod-1 — will monitor. running the rollback command: `infractl pools update x-prod-1 --set scheduler.preemptive_swap=false`

oncall-bot: Deploy started by maria at 14:10 UTC — change id deploy-789. Watchlist: x-prod-1.

maria: rollback completed. avg_batch_size jumped to ~3.8 within two minutes and p95 dropped to 220ms. No new 429s observed in the last 5m.

dinesh: follow-ups: we should
- add a regression test that runs a mixed-short workload against the scheduler change
- fix token accounting so queue_quota scales with effective batch tokens not request count when batching is disabled
- reconsider adaptive token_sort thresholds (maybe require min_queue_depth before reordering)

sam: opened issue INF-6423 with steps and graphs, tagging eng-runtime and eng-platform. link: https://redwood.internal/issue/INF-6423

maria: notifying account exec + CS. Customer impacted for ~7m, will offer credits if needed. Logged customer repro steps and the remediation in INF-6423.

support-bot: Case #ACME-1123 updated: mitigation applied, monitoring green.

jess: long term: add a canary that simulates short-heavy tenant traffic during scheduler config rollouts. Also add an automatic safety that disables preemptive_swap when average batch < 3 for >60s.

maria: thanks all. leaving this thread open for notes; will copy final postmortem to incidents channel once we finish the runbook updates.
